answer: 295 of the 501 faces that state a bar count (58.9%) also publish the rows that count is about, so a duplicated row would show in them; the other 206 publish a number no published data can contradict, and 0 counted faces already publish a duplicated row (0 rows) -- and only 3 of the counted faces print a dedupe field or a distinct count, so even where the rows exist the count itself is not what would catch a duplicate
limits: the count vocabulary and the count-block walker are e597's; a face that states a bar count under a name outside that vocabulary is not in this population
a 'duplicated row' is a repeat of the whole object after a json round-trip; two rows that differ in any field are two rows even if they describe one bar
the distinct-bar read is only published when the series carries one of ['bar', 'date', 'bar_date', 'as_of', 'day', 'trade_date', 'ts', 'time'] as a key
a series longer than 5000 rows is measured on its head; duplicates past that point are not counted
at most 6 series per face are measured, so a face with more than that is graded on its first 6
faces above 1000000 bytes are counted as unreadable rather than parsed
this study reads results/** and docs/** and excludes its own two published files
